result.target_summary: Citi's 2024 net interest income decreased 1% to $54.1 billion ($54.2 billion TEB), primarily due to lower non-Markets income from higher mortgage-backed securities funding costs in Corporate Treasury and lower Argentina investment revenue, partially offset by USPB and Wealth growth. comparisons.peer_topic: Net interest income and yield performance in 2024
comparisons.peer_summary: Net interest income decreased by $871 million to $56.1 billion in 2024 compared to 2023, with net interest yield on a fully taxable-equivalent basis dropping 13 basis points to 1.95 percent. These declines were primarily driven by higher deposit costs, which were partially offset by higher asset yields and increased net interest income from Global Markets activity.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citi and Bank of America reported a decrease in total net interest income in 2024, accompanied by a contraction in net interest margin. Citi's NII decreased by 1% to $54.1 billion with a margin of 2.40% TEB, driven by higher funding costs in Corporate Treasury and lower Argentina revenue. Similarly, Bank of America's NII decreased by $871 million to $56.1 billion, with its FTE net interest yield dropping 13 basis points to 1.95%, primarily driven by higher deposit costs. While Citi highlighted Argentina as a specific drag, BAC cited broader deposit cost pressures, yet both firms experienced margin compression linked to rising funding expenses.

sentences.text: Citi's net interest income for 2024 decreased 1%, or approximately $0.8 billion, to $54.1 billion ($54.2 billion on a taxable equivalent basis) versus the prior year.

In 2024, Citi's net interest margin decreased to 2.40% on a taxable equivalent basis, compared to 2.46% in 2023, primarily driven by lower revenue from Citi's net investment in Argentina and higher funding cost.
Net interest income decreased $871 million to $56.1 billion in 2024 compared to 2023.
Net interest yield on a fully taxable-equivalent (FTE) basis decreased 13 basis points (bps) to 1.95 percent for 2024.
The decreases were primarily driven by higher deposit costs, partially offset by higher asset yields and higher net interest income related to Global Markets activity.

comparisons.peer_topic: Net Interest Income Growth and Drivers
comparisons.peer_summary: Net interest income for 2024 was $8.06 billion, representing a 27% increase from 2023, driven by higher interest income from trading assets, investments, and collateralized agreements due to higher balances and rates, partially offset by a decrease in deposits with banks.
comparisons.comparison: Unlike Citi, which saw a decline in net interest income driven by funding costs and specific regional factors, Goldman Sachs reported a significant 27% increase in net interest income to $8.06 billion in 2024. This divergence is attributed to Goldman's strategic focus on balance sheet expansion in trading assets and investments, which benefited from higher average balances and rates, whereas Citi's performance was weighed down by mortgage-backed securities funding costs in Corporate Treasury and lower Argentina investment revenue.

sentences.text: The decrease was primarily due to a decrease in non-Markets net interest income, largely driven by higher funding costs in the mortgage-backed securities portfolio in Corporate Treasury within All Other and lower revenue from Citi's net investment in Argentina, partially offset by growth in USPB and Wealth.

Net interest income in the consolidated statements of earnings was $8.06 billion for 2024, 27% higher than 2023, reflecting an increase in interest income, partially offset by an increase in interest expense.

The increase in interest income primarily related to trading assets and investments (each reflecting the impact of higher average balances and higher average interest rates), collateralized agreements and other interest-earning assets (each reflecting the impact of higher average interest rates), partially offset by a decrease in interest income related to deposits with banks (reflecting the impact of lower average balances).

comparisons.peer_summary: JPMorganChase reported 2024 net income of $58.5 billion (up 18%), EPS of $19.75, and total net revenue of $177.6 billion (up 12%), driven by 4% growth in Net Interest Income and 23% growth in Noninterest Revenue, which included a $7.9 billion gain from Visa shares.
comparisons.comparison: JPMorgan Chase achieved 4% growth in net interest income to $92.6 billion in 2024, contrasting with Citi's 1% decrease. While Citi's decline was driven by higher funding costs in Corporate Treasury and Argentina-specific issues, JPMorgan's growth was driven by balance sheet actions, higher Card Services balances, and higher Markets net interest income. However, JPMorgan also noted 'deposit margin compression across the lines of business,' indicating some similarity in funding cost pressures, though JPMorgan managed to grow NII while Citi saw a slight contraction.

comparisons.peer_summary: Wealth Management net interest revenues decreased 10% year-over-year to $7,313 million in 2024, primarily driven by lower average sweep deposits, partially offset by higher investment portfolio yields and lending growth.

Similarly, Morgan Stanley's Wealth Management net interest revenues decreased 10% to $7,313 million, primarily due to lower average sweep deposits. While Citi's driver was higher funding costs and MS's was lower deposit volumes, both highlight the sensitivity of net interest income to deposit and funding dynamics in a changing rate environment.
